items.t: Ukraine damages Crimea bridge in record drone attack
items.d: Kyiv's biggest drone strike of the war left a section of the Kerch bridge linking Russia to Crimea collapsed. The Kremlin vows to rebuild; Russian strikes killed at least seven in Ukraine.

items.t: US envoys meet Europeans in Berlin as Trump heads for Xi-Putin summit
items.d: Witkoff and Kushner are holding Ukraine talks in Berlin, while Trump, now in Asia, plans a three-way summit with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday. Moscow still resists a seat for Europe.

items.t: Bahrain intercepts Iranian drone aimed at US radar
items.d: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they hit a US radar at a Bahrain base; Bahrain says it stopped the drone. More ships caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, keeping Gulf tensions high.

items.t: Netanyahu camp faces election-meddling allegations
items.d: Reports say Netanyahu aides tipped off police before the 27 October vote, leading to arrests of Arab party workers. Prime minister-elect Gadi Eisenkot has demanded an inquiry.

items.t: Mongolia's president to resign over bribery claim
items.d: Khurelsukh Ukhnaa said he will step down after an ex-Ulaanbaatar mayor accused him of taking $25m tied to a railway deal. He denies wrongdoing and says he will cooperate.

items.t: Japan scrambles jets as Russian planes enter its airspace
items.d: Tokyo protested after two suspected Russian aircraft crossed into Japanese airspace; South Korea and Taiwan also tracked Russian planes, as Putin travels to Asia.

items.t: Wall Street falls ahead of Nvidia's results
items.d: The Dow dropped about 1.4% and the S&P 500 1% as a Fed official urged rate rises of up to 1.5 points. October US retail sales beat forecasts; Disney and Home Depot also beat.

items.t: Anthropic IPO set to debut Thursday
items.d: The Claude maker's share sale, seeking up to $64bn at about a $1.4tn valuation, is expected to be the largest stock market debut on record.

items.t: China and Canada agree further tariff cuts
items.d: Xi and Carney agreed China will ease duties on about $280m of Canadian goods, while Canada extends exemptions on some Chinese steel and aluminium for two years.

items.t: California sues OpenAI over AI safety
items.d: Attorney General Rob Bonta alleges OpenAI built powerful AI without proper safeguards, citing experimental OpenAI agents that broke into Hugging Face's systems in July. OpenAI says it is being unfairly singled out.

items.t: Nvidia reports tonight, its first results without Huang
items.d: Interim CEO Colette Kress hosts the call after Jensen Huang's shock exit; analysts expect revenue near $109bn. Nvidia's board reportedly won't consider Huang's return.

items.t: US tightens rules on overseas AI data centres
items.d: A new Commerce Department rule makes foreign data centres get a licence before selling large amounts of computing power to firms from China and other high-risk countries.

items.t: Google warns AI-run cyberattacks have crossed a threshold
items.d: A Google threat report says attackers are now using autonomous AI agents to find flaws and break in faster, raising the stakes for defenders.

items.t: Apple launches big study on health chatbots
items.d: Up to 200,000 US iPhone users can join an Apple study, built with OpenEvidence, on how people use and trust AI health advice. Apple says the data won't train AI models.

items.t: Big US data centres emit as much CO2 as Denmark
items.d: A Harvard study in Nature Sustainability estimates the largest US data centres emit about 26m tonnes of CO2 a year, and urges treating them as major industrial sites.

items.t: 128 nations debate banning killer robots at UN
items.d: Talks in Geneva are weighing a treaty on lethal autonomous weapons; the US, Russia and Israel oppose binding rules, with Washington offering voluntary guidelines instead.

items.t: EU courts China to keep climate science reports on time
items.d: At COP31 in Turkey, European officials are seeking Chinese support against an India- and Saudi-led push to delay the IPCC's next big reports, due in 2028.

items.t: UK unemployment falls unexpectedly to 4.6%
items.d: Joblessness dipped in the three months to September, but payrolls and vacancies fell and pay growth slowed to 3.5%, strengthening the case for a Bank of England rate cut.

items.t: Burnham says Brexit has diminished Britain
items.d: In his Lord Mayor's Banquet speech the PM said the UK lost more than it gained by leaving the EU, and signalled closer ties, though on a slower timetable.

items.t: UK sanctions Israeli settlement builders
items.d: Britain is sanctioning eight Israeli construction firms building West Bank settlements and an activist group that blocks aid to Gaza.

items.t: 烏克蘭以史上最大規模無人機襲擊重創克里米亞大橋
items.d: 基輔發動開戰以來最大規模無人機襲擊，連接俄羅斯與克里米亞的刻赤大橋有一段倒塌。克里姆林宮誓言重建；俄軍空襲則在烏克蘭造成最少七死。

items.t: 特朗普赴中俄三方峰會　美特使在柏林與歐洲會談
items.d: 美國特使韋科夫和庫什納在柏林與烏克蘭及歐洲官員商討和談；正在亞洲訪問的特朗普計劃周四在深圳與習近平、普京舉行三方峰會。莫斯科仍反對歐洲參與談判。

items.t: 巴林攔截伊朗攻擊美軍雷達的無人機
items.d: 伊朗革命衛隊聲稱擊中巴林基地的美軍雷達，巴林則指已攔截無人機。霍爾木茲海峽再有船隻起火，海灣局勢持續緊張。

items.t: 內塔尼亞胡陣營被指干預選舉
items.d: 報道指內塔尼亞胡助手在10月27日投票前向警方通風報信，導致阿拉伯政黨工作人員被捕。候任總理艾森科特要求展開調查。

items.t: 蒙古總統涉受賄指控宣布辭職
items.d: 呼日勒蘇赫表示會辭職，此前烏蘭巴托前市長指控他收取與鐵路項目有關的2,500萬美元。他否認違法，並稱會配合調查。

items.t: 俄軍機闖入日本領空　日方緊急派戰機
items.d: 兩架懷疑俄羅斯軍機侵犯日本領空，東京提出抗議；南韓和台灣亦追蹤俄機動向，適逢普京出訪亞洲。

items.t: Nvidia公布業績前美股下跌
items.d: 道指跌約1.4%，標普500指數跌1%，一名聯儲局官員主張加息最多1.5厘。美國10月零售銷售勝預期，迪士尼和家得寶業績亦優於預期。

items.t: Anthropic周四上市
items.d: Claude開發商集資最多640億美元、估值約1.4萬億美元，預料成為史上最大規模的新股上市。

items.t: 中加同意進一步減關稅
items.d: 習近平與加拿大總理卡尼達成協議，中方為約2.8億美元加拿大貨品減免關稅，加方則將部分中國鋼鋁豁免延長兩年。

items.t: 加州起訴OpenAI　指其忽視AI安全
items.d: 加州總檢察長邦塔指OpenAI開發強大AI卻缺乏足夠保障，並引述7月有實驗性OpenAI代理入侵Hugging Face系統。OpenAI稱被不公平針對。

items.t: Nvidia今晚公布黃仁勳離任後首份業績
items.d: 臨時行政總裁Colette Kress主持業績會，分析師預期收入約1,090億美元。據報董事會不考慮讓黃仁勳回巢。

items.t: 美國收緊海外AI數據中心規定
items.d: 美國商務部新規要求海外數據中心向中國等高風險國家企業提供大量算力前，必須先取得許可證。

items.t: Google警告AI自主網絡攻擊已越過臨界點
items.d: Google威脅報告指，攻擊者已利用自主AI代理更快找出漏洞並入侵系統，防守方壓力大增。

items.t: Apple推大型健康AI研究
items.d: 最多20萬名美國iPhone用戶可參與Apple與OpenEvidence合作的研究，了解大眾如何使用和信任AI健康建議。Apple稱數據不會用作訓練AI。

items.t: 美國大型數據中心碳排放媲美丹麥
items.d: 哈佛大學刊於《Nature Sustainability》的研究估計，美國最大型數據中心每年排放約2,600萬噸二氧化碳，建議當作大型工業設施監管。

items.t: 128國在聯合國商討禁止「殺手機械人」
items.d: 日內瓦會議討論禁止致命自主武器的條約；美國、俄羅斯和以色列反對具約束力的規則，美方建議改為自願性指引。

items.t: 歐盟拉攏中國　力保氣候報告如期發表
items.d: 歐洲官員在土耳其COP31會議爭取中方支持，對抗印度和沙特阿拉伯推遲IPCC下一批報告的建議，報告原定2028年發表。

items.t: 英國失業率意外降至4.6%
items.d: 截至9月的三個月失業率回落，但受薪職位和職位空缺減少，薪金增長放緩至3.5%，加強英倫銀行減息的理據。

items.t: 賓咸指脫歐令英國實力削弱
items.d: 首相在倫敦市長晚宴演說中表示，英國脫歐得不償失，並暗示會加強與歐盟關係，但步伐較慢。

items.t: 英國制裁以色列屯墾區建築商
items.d: 英國制裁八間在西岸興建屯墾區的以色列建築公司，以及一個阻撓援助物資進入加沙的激進組織。
